summary: A cats.com article by Jackie Brown listing nine cat breeds with blue eyes, explaining that blue eyes are tied to white coats or the pointed Siamese color pattern and are rarer than other eye colors. It notes that most kittens are born with blue eyes that change with age, and that blue eyes in solid white cats are linked to deafness but not blindness. Each breed entry gives origin, height, weight, lifespan, group, price and eye-color notes, followed by a FAQ and reader comments.
one_line: Cats.com article profiling nine blue-eyed cat breeds, from Balinese and Birman to Siamese and Thai, plus the link between white coats and deafness.
key_facts: Blue eyes in cats are associated with white coats or the pointed color pattern seen in the Siamese and related breeds.
Most kittens are born with blue eyes, which gradually change to their adult color as the kitten grows.
Solid white cats with two blue eyes are deaf in one or both ears in an estimated 65% to 80% of cases.
About 40% of all-white cats with one blue eye are deaf.
Blue eyes in white cats are associated only with deafness, not blindness.
The Balinese is essentially a longhaired Siamese cat and comes in seal, chocolate, blue and lilac pointed colors with deep, vivid blue eyes.
The Birman has four white paws, always has deep, vivid blue eyes, and has a Burma origin with a price range of $400 - $1,000.
The Colorpoint Shorthair was created when some U.S. breeders began experimenting with color in the Siamese breed in the 1940s and 1950s.
The Himalayan is a Persian cat with the pointed coat of a Siamese, created in the 1950s, and its eyes are always blue with deeper blue preferred.
The Ragdoll was created in the 1960s and is known for going limp in your arms like a ragdoll, hence the breed name.
The Siamese is described as the original blue eyed cat breed and likely originated in Siam (present-day Thailand).
An ancient manuscript called the Cat Book of Poems, dating to 1350, contains illustrations of a cat that closely resembles the Siamese.
The Snowshoe was developed in the 1960s by breeding Siamese with a tuxedo American Shorthair and nearly went extinct before bouncing back in the late 1980s.
The Thai is also known as the "old-style Siamese" or "applehead Siamese" and is recognized by TICA but not the CFA.
The FAQ lists at least 10 breeds whose eyes are always blue, including Ojos Azules, and other breeds that sometimes have blue eyes, such as the Turkish Van.

entities.name: Balinese
entities.role: Blue-eyed breed described as a longhaired Siamese, originating in the United States

entities.name: Birman
entities.role: Blue-eyed pointed breed with four white paws, originating in Burma

entities.name: Colorpoint Shorthair
entities.role: Breed essentially a Siamese with more allowable pointed colors, created in the 1940s and 1950s

entities.name: Himalayan
entities.role: Persian cat with the pointed coat of a Siamese, created in the 1950s

entities.name: Javanese
entities.role: Color division within the Balinese breed standard, originating in Canada

entities.name: Ragdoll
entities.role: Large longhaired breed created in the 1960s, known for going limp when held

entities.name: Siamese
entities.role: Original blue eyed cat breed, likely originating in Siam (present-day Thailand)

entities.name: Snowshoe
entities.role: Pointed shorthaired breed with white paws, developed in the 1960s from Siamese and tuxedo American Shorthair

entities.name: Thai
entities.role: Old-style Siamese, also called applehead Siamese, recognized by TICA

entities.name: Cat Book of Poems
entities.role: Ancient manuscript dating to 1350 with an illustration resembling the Siamese

entities.name: Cat Fanciers Association
entities.role: Registry that considers the Colorpoint Shorthair its own breed and includes the Himalayan under the Persian standard

entities.name: The International Cat Association
entities.role: Registry that includes non-traditional Siamese colors within the Siamese Group breed standard

entities.name: TICA
entities.role: Registry that recognizes the Himalayan and Thai as separate breeds

entities.name: CFA
entities.role: Registry that does not recognize the Thai and folds the Himalayan into the Persian standard
